name: Luakit
developer: Aidan Holm, Mason Larobina and contributors
statusNote: Stable releases are infrequent (2.4.0 on Feb 14, 2025), but the develop branch was still receiving commits in May 2026
updateCadence: About one stable release a year (2.3.6 Jan 2024, 2.4.0 Feb 2025); develop branch active through 2026
pitch: Vim-style WebKitGTK browser framework you configure and extend entirely in Lua.
summary: Luakit is a small, keyboard-driven browser on WebKitGTK and GTK, configured in Lua with modal navigation, link hints, an ad blocker and userscripts. It targets Linux and BSD power users who want to script their browser.
bestFor: Vim-style keyboard users who want a scriptable WebKit browser
Linux and BSD users who prefer a tiny GTK-based browser
Tinkerers who want to change behavior with Lua
notFor: Anyone who wants extensions from the Chrome or Firefox stores
People who need Netflix-class DRM video or sync
Windows or mobile users, since there is no native build

pros.title: Lua everywhere
pros.detail: Configure through userconf.lua, a full rc.lua copy or theme.lua, and run Lua at runtime with :lua.

pros.title: Modal keyboard control
pros.detail: Vim-style normal and follow modes with link hints, and :help inside the browser.

pros.title: Built-in blocking and userscripts
pros.detail: An ad blocker with configurable filter lists, plus user stylesheets and userscripts loaded from its directories.

pros.title: Small and packaged
pros.detail: The Arch package installs at 3.6 MB and Debian stable, testing and unstable carry 2.4.0.

pros.title: No telemetry, GPL-3.0
pros.detail: Open source with a public develop branch and CI added in 2026.

cons.title: Slow stable releases
cons.detail: Only about one tagged release a year, so users on distro builds lag the develop branch.

cons.title: Engine limits
cons.detail: WebKitGTK compatibility and speed trail Chromium, and the project says rendering issues usually come from WebKit.

cons.title: No extension stores
cons.detail: No WebExtensions, only Lua modules and userscripts, and no sync or password vault.

cons.title: Steep learning curve
cons.detail: Config in Lua and modal keys are aimed at power users; Windows works only via WSL and is not actively supported.

faq.a: Yes, though stable releases are rare: 2.4.0 shipped Feb 14, 2025 and the develop branch had commits through May 2026, including a JavaScriptCore rewrite of DOM element access.
WebKitGTK (webkit2gtk) with GTK 3; recent versions use webkit2gtk-4.1 and libsoup3.

faq.q: Does Luakit run on Windows or macOS?
faq.a: Linux and BSD are supported; Windows 10 works through WSL but is not actively supported, and no macOS build is listed.

timeline.event: Mason Larobina publicly introduces luakit as a Lua-configurable WebKit browser framework (Arch Linux forum thread)
2.4.0 released (Feb 14) with DOM events via signals and an enable_pdfjs setting
develop branch gains GitHub Actions CI, a JavaScriptCore DOM rewrite and an IPC buffer-overflow fix

switching.note: No importers documented; bookmarks are stored locally and can be copied by hand.

mv2.note: No WebExtensions; Lua modules and userscripts only

privacy.defaults: No telemetry; built-in ad blocker and NoScript-style policy available; WebKit's own protections apply

spec.defaultSearch: Configurable in Lua (custom search engines are easy to add)
spec.drm: Not provided in standard WebKitGTK builds (unverified)
spec.sandbox: WebKitGTK multi-process model; sandbox depends on the distro build (unverified)
spec.patchLag: Follows distro WebKitGTK updates; the site says to keep WebKit up to date for security

linux.minOs: GTK 3, webkit2gtk-4.1, Lua 5.1 or LuaJIT, SQLite 3
notes: Arch extra 2.4.0-3 (built 2026-06-27); Debian stable, testing and unstable at 2.4.0-1
Also packaged for FreeBSD and OpenBSD; Windows 10 via WSL known to work but not supported

trackingProtection: Ad blocker filter lists; no tracker list by default
adBlocker: Built in with configurable filter lists
customFilterLists: Filter lists loaded from the data directory
screenshots: :save writes a single MHTML file, not an image
keyboardShortcuts: Modal keys fully rebindable in Lua
devtools: WebKit inspector, not re-checked in fetched pages

jsSpeed: JavaScriptCore via WebKitGTK, behind Safari tuning
smoothness: WebKitGTK scrolling; changelog notes smooth-scroll quirks
graphics: WebKitGTK GPU path, hardware accel default always
privacyDefaults: No telemetry; blocker and NoScript policy available
securityHardening: WebKitGTK multi-process; IPC overflow fixed in develop
patchSpeed: Depends on distro WebKitGTK; 2.4.0 is dated
behaviourCustom: Rebind everything in Lua, modal keys
extras: Gopher support, MHTML save, ad blocker
longevity: Since 2010, active develop branch, few maintainers

unverified: Exact first-release date: the earliest evidence is a May 2010 Arch Linux forum thread seen via search, with date-based releases from 2010 and 2011
Whether the WebKit Web Inspector is exposed (not confirmed in fetched pages); score and rating are conservative
Sandbox status, DRM absence and codec coverage depend on the distro WebKitGTK build
Default search engine, per-site settings and exact private-browsing behavior
Packaging on Fedora and other rpm distros (only Arch, Debian, Gentoo, FreeBSD and OpenBSD packaging was seen)
No benchmark numbers were found; speed scores are editorial relative to GNOME Web and qutebrowser
